narrative.text: NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants. It has a collaboration with Cisco to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms. NVIDIA Corporation was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

base.writtenAnchor: Demand stays strong but normalises off an enormous base. The July 2026 quarter was still running 105.9% ahead of the year-ago quarter with trailing revenue of 303.0bn, so the near-term run-rate is well above the FY2026 reported year (H:quarter, H:revenue); growth then decelerates sharply as the base compounds, settling at a high-teens constant rate for years 1-5. Operating margin holds in the mid-50s — below the 62.4% peak of FY2025 and the 60.4% of FY2026, reflecting mix shift into full systems and networking, but far above the 33.0% median of the longer history (H:margin). New capital keeps earning well: the last five years' incremental return on new capital was 75.2%, and the base case assumes roughly half of that persists before fading to the terminal return (H:returns). Net reinvestment stays light relative to revenue, as capex of 6.0bn against 2.8bn of depreciation on 215.9bn of revenue shows (H:capex).

bear.writtenAnchor: The AI build-out that drove revenue from 60.9bn in FY2024 to 215.9bn in FY2026 proves to be a pull-forward: hyperscale customers digest the capacity they have bought, and NVIDIA's own filed history shows how fast this business can stall — revenue grew 0.2% in FY2023 and operating margin collapsed to 15.7% that year (H:revenue, H:margin). Growth flattens to low single digits off a very large base, pricing concessions and a heavier mix of lower-margin systems pull margin back toward the mid-30s, and the capital already deployed (invested capital rose from 45.4bn to 155.2bn in two years) earns far less than the 66-81% returns of the boom (H:returns). Stock compensation of 6.4bn a year keeps leaking share count (H:cashflow).

bull.writtenAnchor: Accelerated computing keeps absorbing a growing share of global data-centre spend and NVIDIA holds its position across silicon, networking and software. Revenue compounds near 30% a year off a base that already grew 105.9% year-on-year in the latest quarter (H:quarter), operating margin returns toward the FY2025 peak of 62.4% as scale and software mix offset system costs (H:margin), and incremental capital keeps earning close to the 75.2% incremental return of the last five years and the 81.2% peak ROIC (H:returns). Operating cash flow of 102.7bn funds growth internally and lets repurchases absorb the 6.4bn annual stock-compensation charge, holding share count flat (H:cashflow).
